docs.title: Gathering
docs.text:
task gather                                  # lists, and metadata of the newest year, every journal
task gather -- 2025 2026                     # metadata of these years
task gather -- --all                         # metadata of every year
task gather -- 2026 --acts --limit 5         # and all files of the first 5 acts that miss any
task gather -- 2026 --parts pdf,html         # only these files
task gather -- --publisher MP                # one journal (DU, MP); can be repeated
task gather -- 2026 --acts --rate 60         # slower: 60 requests per minute
task gather:everything                       # everything the API has; asks before it starts
task gather:changes                          # acts changed since the previous such run
task gather:changes -- 2026-10-01            # acts changed since that day

The source is the ELI API of Sejm, https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli. It is an open API, so the gatherer uses plain requests, with no browser, and says who it is in the User-Agent.

docs.title: What one run does
docs.text:
first walk
GET /                  index: names of everything the API gives
 └─ every list_*       statuses, types, reference types, keywords, institutions, journals
     └─ journals       DU and MP, each with its years
         └─ year       every act of the year, in one answer

second walk, one year after another
year ── act            the files that are not here yet
         └─ texts      other texts of the act, named in its details
  1. The index is saved as dataset/lists/index.json, and every list it names as dataset/lists/<name>.json.
  2. The list of journals opens the years: the newest one, the years you named, or all of them with --all.
  3. Each year is saved as dataset/acts/<journal>/<year>.jsonl, one act per line, sorted by position.
  4. With --acts or --parts, the files of acts are taken into bucket/<journal>/<year>/, a year at a time. See the data for what each file holds.
  5. Every file that lands gets a record with its checksum in dataset/files/<journal>/<year>.jsonl.

docs.title: Files of an act
docs.text:
Part File Exists for details <address>.json every act references <address>.references.json every act pdf <address>.pdf acts with textPDF html <address>.html acts with textHTML struct <address>.struct.json acts with textHTML texts <address>.T.pdf, <address>.U.pdf acts whose details name more texts

--acts takes all of them. texts are read from the details of the act, so the details have to be here or be asked for in the same run.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning years, as plain numbers the newest year which years. A year the journal does not have is dropped --all off every year of the journal --publisher DU every journal which journal. Can be repeated --acts off take every file of each act --parts details,pdf none take only these files --limit 20 20 how many acts one run takes files for. 0 means no limit --rate 120 120 requests per minute --since 2026-10-01 off only acts changed since that day, or last

Without --acts and --parts, only lists and listings are gathered.

docs.title: When is a file "here"
docs.text:
A file is not asked for when either is true:

  • it lies in resources/bucket/;
  • it has a record in dataset/files/.

The second rule is for a machine that has the dataset and not the bucket: it does not ask Sejm again for what the bucket already keeps.

Remember! If you delete a file to take it again, delete its lines in dataset/files/<journal>/<year>.jsonl too. With the record in place the file counts as gathered.

docs.title: Stopping and starting again
docs.text:
Stop it with Ctrl+C and start the same command again. It lists the years again and takes what is missing. Nothing has to be resumed: what is gathered is known from the files.

The gatherer keeps its queue of requests in memory and writes nothing to storage/. The message about CRAWLEE_PURGE_ON_START that Crawlee prints when interrupted does not apply here. A storage/ directory left by earlier versions can be deleted.

--limit counts acts that miss at least one file, in order of journals and years. So --limit 5 repeated five times takes 25 acts.

docs.title: Changes at the source
docs.text:
Sejm changes the records of old acts all the time: a status when an act is repealed, new references when an act is amended. Between 12 and 13 October 2026 it changed 81 acts.

task gather:changes -- 2026-10-01     # the first time, with a day
task gather:changes                   # later: since the newest change seen before

It asks the API which acts changed, lists their years again, and takes the details and references of those acts again. With --acts or --parts after the day it takes those files instead. The published PDF is never taken twice, because a published text does not change.

A file whose content really changed gets a new record in dataset/files/; the old record stays above it, so the history of a file can be read.

The date to continue from is kept in dataset/lists/changes.json. It is written only when the run finished without being cut by --limit.

Remember! A year's listing is written again on every run, so it is always as fresh as the last run that listed that year. Details are as fresh as the last gather:changes.

docs.title: What it never does
docs.text:
• It does not ask for texts that do not exist. The listing says which acts have a PDF or an HTML. The API answers a missing HTML with status 200 and an empty page, so the flags are trusted.
  • It does not treat "the source has none" as an error. A 404 is logged and nothing is written.
  • It does not leave half a file. A file is written as <name>.part and renamed when complete. After an interrupted run, .part files can be deleted.
  • It does not accept a wrong answer as a PDF. A PDF must start with %PDF, and an empty text is an error.
  • It does not write outside its directory. Names of files come from the answers of the API. An act or a text whose name could leave the directory is refused.
  • It does not hurry. Two requests at a time. --rate sets the pace per minute.

docs.title: How big it is
docs.text:
Counts from the list of journals on 2026-10-13:

Journal Acts Years DU, Dziennik Ustaw 97,907 1918 to 2026, without 1940 to 1943 MP, Monitor Polski 66,730 1930 to 2026

The listings say 164,499 acts have a PDF and 39,110 have an HTML, all of the latter in Dziennik Ustaw. Everything is then about 572 thousand requests, plus the other texts, whose number is known only from details: at 120 per minute, more than three days without a break.

The first sixteen years of Dziennik Ustaw (1918 to 1933, 11 thousand acts) took 10 GB in 34 thousand files. (The total size is not known yet.)

docs.title: When something fails
docs.text:
What you see What it means DU/1950 is cut: 500 of 800 the API gave only a part of the year. Not seen so far; if it happens, report it as a bug ... source does not have it the API answered 404. Nothing is written; the next run asks again ... is empty the listing promised a text and the API gave none. The crawler retries, then gives up on that file ... did not answer with pdf something else came in place of a PDF, usually an error page act with unusable name the API gave an act whose address cannot be a file name. Report it as a bug requests fail in a row the API may be down or limiting. Stop, wait, lower --rate, start again

Failed files are simply missing afterwards, so the next run asks for them again.

docs.title: Moving data to Hugging Face
docs.text:
task resources:plan -- dataset     # what differs; changes nothing
task resources:pull -- dataset     # take files that are there and not here
task resources:push -- dataset     # send files that are new or changed here; asks first
task resources:push -- bucket --batch 500   # commits of 500 files
task resources:prune -- space      # delete there what is not here; asks first; never the bucket

The name after -- is a key of resources/.map.json:

Name Local side On Hugging Face dataset resources/dataset datasets/Sarverott/polish_national_law_docs bucket resources/bucket buckets/Sarverott/raw-law-of-poland space resources/space spaces/Sarverott/docs-of-law-by-gov-in-poland conversations resources/conversations datasets/Apokryf/Consiliariis-Polonicum-Lex - the mastermind's conversations (phase 31); its card is resources/conversations/README.md, kept in git

The local sides are ignored by git of this repository.

docs.title: How it decides what to move
docs.text:
The two sides are compared file by file:

  1. by path;
  2. by size;
  3. when both agree, by content: the hash git gives to a file, or SHA-256 for big files kept in LFS. The local file is read only at this step.
The file is plan calls it push pull here and not there upload sends it leaves it there and not here download leaves it takes it on both sides, different changed sends the local one leaves the local one and names it on both sides, the same same nothing nothing

So repeating a push costs one listing and moves only what is new. Nothing is moved twice.

Remember! A bucket gives no hash. There a file counts as the same when path and size agree. A file that changed without changing its size would be missed. The project keeps its own checksums for that: task seal -- --check compares every file here with the record made when it was gathered. See processing.

docs.title: What it never does
docs.text:
• push never deletes a file on Hugging Face. A file removed here stays there - until prune is asked for by name.
  • pull never overwrites a local file.
  • .git, node_modules, .venv, __pycache__ and .part files are never moved in any direction.

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
Needs HF_TOKEN in the environment or in .env, with write access.

Files go in commits of 1000, titled P-jol-roll: 1000 files (3000 of 14170). --batch changes the number. A repository on Hugging Face takes at most 128 commits an hour; when it refuses one, the push says how long it waits, waits and sends the same commit again (with commits of 100, a push of 14170 files stopped at the 128th). If a push stops in the middle, start it again: the commits already made are on the other side, and the comparison skips their files.

docs.title: Prune
docs.text:
task resources:prune -- space deletes on Hugging Face every file that is there and not here - the files plan lists as download. Look at them first with task resources:plan -- space. It goes in commits of 1000, waits out the hourly limit as push does, and asks before it starts. It refuses the bucket: raw files may live on one machine only.

It was made for the space, which kept app.py, development.md and requirements.txt of its marimo days after it became a Docker space. On the dataset, prune only after a pull, or it deletes what this machine never took.

docs.title: The space after a release
docs.text:
A restart of the space builds nothing new: Hugging Face keeps the image it had. Since phase 22 the release is not written into the space's Dockerfile: it is kept in git as resources/configs/space/Dockerfile and takes the release as a build argument, P_JOL_ROLL_VERSION. Hugging Face passes the variables of a space to its build as build arguments, so a release sets that variable and asks for a fresh build:

task resources:space               # the space's files of resources/configs/space into resources/space
task resources:space:refresh       # its files from git when they differ, the variable, a fresh build, waited for (HF_TOKEN)

The release workflow runs the refresh by itself after the image is on ghcr.io. Since phase 27 it also brings the space's own files from git (Dockerfile, and hub/README.md as its README.md) when they differ, and waits until the space runs and its /openapi.json names the release - a build that fails, or takes more than 25 minutes, fails the release with Hugging Face's own message. Its token is the space's trusted publisher: the job has id-token: write, and GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged on https://huggingface.co/oauth/token for a token of this one space, valid an hour; no secret is kept for it. The secret HF_TOKEN stays the fallback. With neither the job says so and the space keeps what it has. resources/configs/space/space.env names the space and may pin a release; an environment variable wins over it (P_JOL_ROLL_VERSION=0.18.0 task resources:space:refresh).

The space mounts the bucket at /data, the place where the image keeps its cache and logs by default. Its Dockerfile moves both to /tmp (RESOURCES_DIR, LOG_DIR); without that line every page read is written into the bucket as resources/ and logs/ (phase 20).

docs.title: Which data goes where
docs.text:
Tables go to the dataset and raw files of acts go to the bucket.

A dataset on Hugging Face is a git repository. Xet, the storage behind it, solves the size of files: big files are cut into chunks, a chunk that was already sent is not sent again, and git keeps only a small pointer. It does not change how many files git has to track. The recommendations of Hugging Face for a git repository still stand (read on 2026-10-13):

What Recommended files in a repository under 100 thousand entries in one folder under 10 thousand files in one commit under 100

A bucket is object storage on the same Xet, without git, and that page says these recommendations do not apply to buckets. So the raw files (several per act, 164 thousand acts) belong in the bucket, and the dataset gets a year in a file wherever it can.

task text writes one markdown file per act with HTML. The listings say 39,110 acts have HTML (all in Dziennik Ustaw, counted on 2026-10-13), in folders of a year each, so the dataset stays inside these recommendations. Parsing of PDF came in phase 12: with task text -- --pdf almost every act gets a markdown file, about 164 thousand files, and the texts should then be packed a year in a file: Q16 of the devlog asks it before they are pushed.

docs.title: What was tested
docs.text: plan was run against the real dataset and bucket. push and pull were not run against Hugging Face: their comparison is covered by tests, and the upload and download calls are not. Try push first on a small directory.

docs.title: Before this
docs.text: The first version cloned the repositories with git, and scripts/hf-push.py sent a whole folder. Both are replaced by src/core/resources/hub.ts. resources/dataset and resources/space may still hold a .git directory from then; it is skipped.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Thing Why Node.js 24 or newer, npm 11 or newer everything runs on it (the code is TypeScript, run with tsx); .nvmrc says 24, engines in package.json says the same git to clone; the repository has one submodule, the Obsidian plugin about 1 GB of disk dependencies, and the Camoufox browser that npm install downloads for checkup Task, optional shorter commands. A copy comes with the dependencies: npx task

Disk for the data is a separate matter: see how big it is.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Sarverott/P-jol-roll.git
cd P-jol-roll
npm install
task verify

npm install also downloads the browser (camoufox-js fetch) and sets up the git hooks (husky). task verify runs the Biome check, the build and the tests. The tests ask nothing on the internet.

Then try a small gathering:

task gather -- 2026 --acts --limit 5

It writes the lists and the listing of 2026 into resources/dataset/ and the files of five acts into resources/bucket/.

docs.title: Without Task
docs.text:
Every task is one npm script underneath:

With Task Without task gather -- 2026 npm run gather -- 2026 task checkup -- 2026 npm run checkup -- 2026 task resources:plan -- dataset npm run hub -- plan dataset task verify npx biome check && npm run build && npx vitest run

docs.title: Token for Hugging Face
docs.text:
Only sending data needs it. Reading public repositories does not.

echo "HF_TOKEN=hf_..." > .env

.env is ignored by git. The token needs write access to the repositories listed in resources/.map.json. See Hugging Face.

docs.title: Settings from the environment
docs.text:
Tasks read them from .env of the working copy too (a variable set in the shell wins).

Variable Default What it changes ELI_API https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli where gather asks. Tests point it at a local copy RESOURCES_DIR resources where everything is written and read HF_TOKEN none token for hub push and for private repositories SEJM_API, SAOS_API the real addresses the same for sejm and saos CRAWLEE_STORAGE_DIR storage where the browser of checkup keeps its queue while it runs. The gatherers keep theirs in memory

docs.title: The Obsidian vault
docs.text: The repository is also an Obsidian vault: open its directory in Obsidian to read the docs with links. .obsidian/plugins/hefaisto is a separate repository (Sarverott/hefaisto). Nothing in gathering depends on it.

docs.title: The law mastermind
docs.text: The first voice of the law mastermind (phase 30; the owner's plan in Q18): a question in words, answered by a model that reads the acts through the project's own MCP tools and cites every act it leans on by its ELI. Not (formally) legal advices: a devil's advocate everyone can afford.

docs.title: How it answers
docs.text:
1. The acts nearest by meaning. The question becomes a vector of the model that made the vectors of task embed (bge-m3), and the MCP tool search_meaning compares it with the vector of every act of every year.
  2. Their texts. The texts of the nearest three (act_text) are read and given to the model with the question.
  3. Rounds. The model may call any tool - act, act_text, search_acts, search_meaning, ... - for at most six rounds, then answers.
  4. The citations checked. Every [DU/<year>/<position>] of the answer is marked read when the model opened that act through a tool, and not read when it named it from memory.

docs.title: On this machine: the host's Ollama
docs.text:
Development uses the Ollama of the host (http://127.0.0.1:11434) and its GPU, with deepseek-r1:8b and bge-m3 pulled into it:

task mastermind:ask -- "Kto płaci podatek dochodowy od osób fizycznych?"
task mastermind:ask -- --json "..."        # with the reasoning and the tools it called
MASTERMIND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434 task serve
curl -G http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/ask --data-urlencode "question=..."

docs.title: On another machine: compose
docs.text:
The profile mastermind brings everything as containers: llms-ollama, llms-models (pulls the models once, then ends), and mastermind - the image of webapp-server with a mastermind set, serving /api/ask, /mcp and the viewer on 127.0.0.1:8081.

task resources:pull -- dataset             # the acts and their vectors (dataset/embeddings/)
task mastermind:up                         # the GPU given to Ollama when nvidia-smi answers
docker compose logs -f llms-models         # the first start downloads about 6 GB
curl -G http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/ask --data-urlencode "question=..."
task mastermind:down

By hand: docker compose --profile mastermind up -d, and -f compose.yaml -f resources/services/gpu.yaml before --profile for the NVIDIA cards (the NVIDIA Container Toolkit is needed for them).

docs.title: The advanced strategy: a deepseek hosted by Hugging Face
docs.text:
The owner's plan (Q18, phase 34): small models on the host first, the hard questions to a large deepseek hosted by Hugging Face. src/mastermind/strategy.ts:

  • --escalate: the usual model answers first; its answer goes on when it is weak - it says nothing, cites no act, or cites an act it never opened. The large one, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 through Inference Providers (https://router.huggingface.co/v1; novita, deepinfra and featherless-ai serve it), gets the small one's answer to check, never to trust, and reads the acts itself through the same MCP tools.
  • --hard: straight to it.
task mastermind:ask -- --escalate "Czy mogę odliczyć ulgę na dziecko po rozwodzie?"
task mastermind:ask -- --hard "..."
curl -G http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/ask --data-urlencode "question=..." -d escalate=1

Here it is paid by HF_TOKEN of .env - the owner's own, so only a question the owner asks spends it; on the space by the signed-in visitor's token. The chat shows a switch a hard question when the host can pay for it (hard of /api/ask/about), and folds what the smaller model said first. The large one's conversation is kept with escalated: the small model, why its answer went on, what it said and where that is kept.

Variable Default What it is HARD_MODEL deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 the model of hard questions HARD_URL https://router.huggingface.co/v1 its OpenAI-like api HARD_KEY HF_TOKEN the token it is paid by

Not yet seen answering for real: Inference Providers refuse the owner's token with 402 until it has credits (phase 32); it is tested against a stand-in of them.

docs.title: The Python stack
docs.text: The models and the simulations have a stack of their own (phase 34): stacks/python/, a uv project reading the law through the same MCP tools (Law) and asking the mastermind through /api/ask (Mastermind). task python:check, task python:law -- nearest "obowiązek szkolny".

docs.title: The executive agent
docs.text:
Not a chat but a task (phase 33): a small qwen does what a person gives it, reading the law through the MCP tools, and writes what it is asked for into resources/agent/ - the only place it can write; it runs no command and fetches no page.

task agent -- "Przeczytaj dekret DU/1919/147 i zapisz w pliku obowiazek-szkolny-1919.md streszczenie"
task agent:container -- "..."     # the same in the agents' shell, with Ollama of the profile llms

Its first real task, on this machine: it read the school decree of 1919 and wrote resources/agent/obowiazek-szkolny-1919.md - school age from 7, seven years of school, to 14 - citing the articles, the act marked read. Every run is kept as a conversation (resources/conversations/qwen/...).

Two engines (AGENT_ENGINE):

  • own (the default): the mastermind's rounds with the MCP tools given directly, and one tool of its own, write_note (a bare file name, markdown, never outside resources/agent/); its instructions are resources/configs/mastermind/executive.md.
  • opencode: opencode 2 as its host, as planned, from resources/configs/agentic-shell/opencode/ - its own config and data directories (resources/.containerdatavol/agent/), so neither the person's opencode settings nor sessions are touched, --standalone, a model of its own with a 24k context. Not yet reliable: opencode 2 hands an MCP server's tools over through Code Mode, and in some runs it does not find the server's namespace (Unknown tool 'p-jol-roll.act_text').
Variable Default What it is AGENT_MODEL qwen3:8b the model AGENT_OLLAMA_URL http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 its Ollama (http://llms-ollama:11434/v1 in the shell) AGENT_ENGINE own own or opencode AGENT_ROUNDS, AGENT_CONTEXT 8, 24576 rounds of tools (own); context of its model (opencode)

docs.title: Ollama on its own drive
docs.text:
The models are large and many, so the Ollama of this machine keeps them on a drive of their own: OLLAMA_MODELS in .env (the variable Ollama itself reads) names the directory.

task ollama:where        # where they are read from, and how many are there
task ollama:serve        # the first start copies ~/.ollama/models there, then serves from there
task ollama:copy         # the copy again: only what is missing, then checked

The old directory is never deleted by them. Stop the Ollama that runs first (ss -ltnp | grep 11434 shows it). A drive whose root belongs to root needs its directory made once: task ollama:serve says the sudo line.

docs.title: The conversations kept
docs.text:
Every question is kept with everything said, so models and families can be compared:

resources/conversations/<family>/<instance>/<UNIXUSAT>-<the question's first words>.json
resources/conversations/deepseek/deepseek-r1-8b/1795498362594-czym-byla-rada-stanu-w-1918-roku.json

The family comes from resources/configs/mastermind/families.yaml (the models of one family act as one team: gemma4, translategemma, embeddinggemma, shieldgemma... are all gemma); the instance is the model with its size. A file holds the question, the answer, the reasoning, the acts cited, the tools called, how long it took and the whole exchange - the texts given and what the tools answered. The directory is the local side of their own dataset, Apokryf/Consiliariis-Polonicum-Lex (conversations of resources/.map.json): task resources:push -- conversations sends what is new, a person's move; git keeps only its card. MASTERMIND_KEEP=0 keeps nothing. In compose it is the one directory the mastermind writes.

docs.title: Families as teams
docs.text:
resources/configs/mastermind/families.yaml names the families and their teams: one model answers, one calls the tools in the rounds, one turns an answer given in another language into the question's, one guards (its verdict kept, nothing held back). A model is given thinking and tools only when Ollama says it can take them.

MASTERMIND_TEAM=gemma task mastermind:ask -- "..."   # gemma4 answers, functiongemma calls tools,
                                                     # translategemma translates, shieldgemma guards
task mastermind:compare                              # every team, the questions of questions.yaml
task mastermind:compare -- bielik qwen               # only these
task resources:push -- conversations                 # what they said, to their dataset

The first comparison (phase 31, 30 answers):

Team Models A question Acts cited (read) What its answers were like gemma gemma4:12b, functiongemma:270m, translategemma:4b, shieldgemma:2b 65-150 s 8 (6) the closest to the text: the twelve virilists of DU/1918/2 named one by one; once "the acts do not answer" in English (the check of Polish then missed it - fixed); the slowest, four models taking turns on 12 GB; functiongemma called no tool in any round deepseek deepseek-r1:8b 31-69 s 10 (9) broken Polish, words of no language mistral ministral-3:8b 14-44 s 11 (10) fast, clear Polish with headings, citing what it read qwen qwen3:8b 20-52 s 13 (12) fluent, cites articles (art. 12) llama llama3.1:8b 8-46 s 2 (2) the fastest; three answers of five cite nothing bielik Bielik 11B v3.0 Q4_K_M 16-57 s 8 (6) the most natural Polish; adds what it knows beyond the acts read (the Council dissolved on 7 October 1918 - true, but not from them)

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default What it is MASTERMIND_URL OLLAMA_URL the model's api: an Ollama, or an OpenAI-like one ending in /v1 (LiteLLM of the profile llms); set on an api, it makes /api/ask answer MASTERMIND_TEAM a team of families.yaml (gemma, bielik, ...) MASTERMIND_MODEL the team's answer, else deepseek-r1:8b the model that answers MASTERMIND_KEY a key for an OpenAI-like api MASTERMIND_ROUNDS 6 rounds of tools at most MASTERMIND_CONTEXT 16384 the context of an Ollama model, in tokens MASTERMIND_WORDS 4096 tokens it may write, thinking too MASTERMIND_READ 6000 characters of one tool's answer kept MASTERMIND_FIRST 3 texts of the nearest acts read before it speaks MASTERMIND_PORT, OLLAMA_PORT 8081, 11434 the ports of compose

docs.title: On the demo space: the visitor's own Hugging Face
docs.text:
The tab ask the law of the viewer (#ask) is the same mastermind as a chat: every cited act a link to its page, the acts it named without reading them marked with ?, its reasoning folded.

On the demo space (phase 32) it runs on the visitor's own account, as the owner's other space does: the space's card asks for hf_oauth with the scope inference-api, the visitor signs in with Hugging Face (/login), and the token stays in the server's memory behind an HttpOnly cookie - it never reaches the browser, a file or a log. Then:

  • the model through Inference Providers (https://router.huggingface.co/v1), google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it by default (DEMO_MODEL; DEMO_URL for another api), paid from the visitor's credits;
  • the question a vector by BAAI/bge-m3 on Hugging Face, the same model as the vectors of the dataset, which the space takes on its first question (about 760 MB);
  • one question at a time per visitor, four at once in all; a visitor's conversation is not kept.

A visitor without credits left gets Hugging Face's own answer: "Purchase pre-paid credits to continue using Inference Providers". The space signs in nobody without hf_oauth in its card, and /api/ask then says so.

Variable Default What it is DEMO_MODEL google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it the model on the space DEMO_URL https://router.huggingface.co/v1 its OpenAI-like api OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, OPENID_PROVIDER_URL, SPACE_HOST set by Hugging Face signing in

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text: deepseek-r1:8b on an RTX 3060 answers in 30 seconds to a few minutes, most of it thinking. It is the smallest voice of the plan: it now and then answers in English, slips a word of another script into Polish, or cites an act it did not open - which the check marks. The larger deepseek of phase 34 (the advanced strategy above) is for the hard questions.

docs.title: The repository on five more places
docs.text:
Phase 46, the owner's order: the repository mirrored on Bitbucket, GitLab, sourcehut, gitea.com and a Gitea of our own, each with the same rules as GitHub - its milestones, its devlog.

Place Code Devlog (milestones, issues) github.com/Sarverott/P-jol-roll the source task github:devlog, devlog.yml gitea.com/Sarverott/P-jol-roll every branch and tag written (Gitea's API) gitlab.com/Sarverott/P-jol-roll every branch and tag written (GitLab's API) bitbucket.org/apokryf/p-jol-roll every branch and tag - Bitbucket Cloud's issues have no milestones git.sr.ht/~sarverott/P-jol-roll every branch and tag - sourcehut's tracker is todo.sr.ht, a service of its own our own Gitea (MIRROR_OWN_GITEA_URL) every branch and tag written (Gitea's API)

The workflow mirrors.yml does it on every push to development: each repository made where it is not, every branch and tag pushed (deletions too), the devlog written, a status badge per place on the branch badges (the README shows them). A mirror whose secret is not set is left out and said; one that fails shows 403 FORBIDDEN on its badge and the run goes on. Pull requests, checks and releases happen on GitHub; the mirrors receive what was merged.

task mirrors                         # the same from here, with the tokens in the environment
MIRRORS_ONLY=own-gitea task mirrors  # one place
task mirror:gitea:up                 # our own Gitea, the compose profile gitea, on 127.0.0.1:3000
task unittesting:mirrors-gitea       # our own Gitea in a container: pushed, devlog written twice the same

docs.title: What the owner sets
docs.text: Secrets of the repository on GitHub (Q21): MIRROR_GITEA_TOKEN, MIRROR_GITLAB_TOKEN, MIRROR_BITBUCKET_TOKEN (an access token of the repository, or an Atlassian API token), MIRROR_SOURCEHUT_SSH_KEY (a private key whose public one sourcehut knows), MIRROR_OWN_GITEA_TOKEN; the variable MIRROR_OWN_GITEA_URL. The repositories on Bitbucket and sourcehut are made by hand once; Gitea and GitLab ones are made by the workflow.

docs.title: Mirrors on a WireGuard network
docs.text: The second step of M5, no centre (phase 38): the law served by mirrors - one per voivodeship, more per district - each a whole copy, joined to the others by WireGuard, the site balanced over all of them by Traefik. No mirror is the centre: each balances over every mirror it knows.

docs.title: The registry
docs.text:
resources/configs/mirrors/mirrors.yaml, in git, is what the mirrors share: the sixteen voivodeships, each at 10.42.<TERYT code>.1 on the network (mazowieckie 10.42.14.1); a district is added with an address of its own. A mirror is on the network once its public key is there.

task mirror:list                    # the mirrors, their addresses, which are on the network

docs.title: A machine becomes a mirror
docs.text:
task mirror:keys -- mazowieckie     # its WireGuard keys: the private one stays in resources/secrets/wireguard/,
                                    # the public one is written into the registry - commit it
task mirror:up -- mazowieckie       # its WireGuard and Traefik made from the registry, then compose up
curl http://127.0.0.1:8095/api/host # the site, answered by any mirror on the network
task mirror:down

The profile mirror of compose runs three containers in one network namespace (WireGuard's): mirror-wireguard, mirror-server (the api over its own resources/) and mirror-traefik. Traefik balances every request over the api of every mirror on the network, through the tunnels, checking each by /api/host; a mirror that does not answer is left out until it does. With a domain in the registry, each mirror is also at <name>.<domain>.

A mirror with an endpoint (host:51820, its UDP port open to the internet) is reached by the others; one without it only calls out, and is reached once it has. When the registry changes - a new mirror, a new key - each mirror runs task mirror:up again.

docs.title: Checked here
docs.text:
task unittesting:mirrors makes two mirrors from a registry of two, in containers: their keys (the same public keys as wg pubkey derives), a real WireGuard tunnel between them, a stand-in of the api in each, and Traefik in one answering from both. 8 s.

Running mirrors on machines in the voivodeships is the owner's: the machines, their addresses, their keys.

docs.title: From raw files to tables and texts
docs.text:
task seal                 # checksums for gathered files that have no record yet
task seal -- --check      # read every recorded file again, name the ones that differ
task compile              # tables: details and references of acts, a year in a file
task text                 # markdown from gathered HTML, with checksums
task text -- --pdf        # and from the PDFs of acts without HTML (poppler-utils)

None of these asks anything on the internet. They read resources/bucket/ and write into resources/dataset/. Each can be repeated at any time.

docs.title: Checksums: seal
docs.text:
A bucket on Hugging Face gives no checksum of a file, so the project keeps its own. One line per file in dataset/files/<journal>/<year>.jsonl:

{"path":"DU/1918/WDU19180010001.json","size":3578,"sha256":"0c1f2c7e...","url":"https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/1918/1","gatheredAt":"2026-10-13T13:25:12.282Z"}
Field Meaning path the file, inside the bucket size, sha256 of the file as it was written url where it was taken from gatheredAt when

The gatherer writes the record at the moment a file lands on disk, before anything is sent anywhere. task seal is for files gathered before records existed: it writes the missing records, with the file's modification time as gatheredAt.

task seal -- --check reads every recorded file that is here and compares. It prints the paths that differ and ends with an error when there are any. Run it after pulling the bucket to another machine, or before a big push.

When a file has several records, the last one is the current one.

docs.title: Tables: compile
docs.text:
Details and references sit in the bucket as one small file per act. For reading in bulk they are put together, a year in a file:

Table One line is Made from dataset/details/<journal>/<year>.jsonl the details of one act, as the API gave them <address>.json dataset/references/<journal>/<year>.jsonl one tie between two acts field references of the details

A line of the references table:

{"from":"DU/1918/2","type":"Uchylenia wynikające z","to":"DU/1918/23","date":"1918-10-21"}
Field Meaning from ELI of the act whose details name the tie type kind of the tie, from lists/reference_types.json to ELI of the other act date, art present when the API gives them

All the references tables together are the graph of the law: which act changes, repeals or carries out which. The first sixteen years of Dziennik Ustaw give 45,658 ties for 11,008 acts.

Acts whose details are not gathered yet are left out. Tables are written whole on every run.

docs.title: Texts: text
docs.text:
Every gathered HTML becomes a markdown file, dataset/texts/<journal>/<year>/<address>.md, and a line in dataset/texts/<journal>/<year>.jsonl ties it to its source:

{"ELI":"DU/1918/2","markdown":"texts/DU/1918/WDU19180020002.md","sha256_md":"a85ee287...","sha256_html":"1fd223bc...","url":"https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/1918/2/text.html"}
Field Meaning markdown the markdown file, inside the dataset sha256_md checksum of the markdown sha256_html checksum of the HTML it was made from url the HTML at the source

An HTML whose checksum did not change is not parsed again.

What the markdown looks like:

# Ustawa z dnia 4 lutego 1918 r. o Radzie Stanu Królestwa Polskiego

## Treść ustawy

### Art. 1.

Rada Stanu Królestwa Polskiego z siedzibą w mieście stołecznem Warszawie składa się ze 110 członków, a mianowicie:

a) 12 członków wirylistów,

Articles, paragraphs (§) and chapters are headings. Points and letters open their own line. Scripts and buttons of Sejm's reader are removed.

Remember! The markdown was looked at only on acts from 1918 to 1933. Newer acts may use HTML this parser has not met, and tables are not turned into markdown tables. Read a few new ones before trusting it in bulk.

Only HTML is parsed: 39,110 of 164,638 acts have it, all in Dziennik Ustaw. The other three quarters have only a PDF and get no markdown yet.

docs.title: Order of work
docs.text: gather ──► seal (once, for old files) ──► compile ──► text ──► resources:push

docs.title: Texts of PDFs
docs.text:
task text -- --pdf gives markdown to acts that have only a PDF. The text layer is read by pdftotext of poppler (scripts/install.sh installs poppler-utils), which follows the two columns of a journal's page. Lines become paragraphs, a word cut at the end of a line is glued back, and Art. 1., § 1. and Rozdział 1 become headings, as in markdown from HTML. Four PDFs are read at a time (--parallel); a year of 1200 acts takes a few seconds.

Most PDFs before the 2000s are scans that Adobe's Paper Capture gave a layer of recognised text. That text is kept as it is, with its mistakes: nothing is corrected by guessing. The record names the producer of the PDF, so a reader can tell these texts apart:

{"ELI":"DU/1953/228","markdown":"texts/DU/1953/WDU19530460228.md","sha256_md":"...","from":"pdf","sha256_pdf":"...","producer":"Adobe Acrobat 9.0 Paper Capture Plug-in","url":"https://api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/1953/228/text.pdf"}

A PDF with no text layer (fewer than 40 letters on all its pages, about one in a hundred) gets no markdown; it is named in dataset/texts/<journal>/<year>.scans.jsonl and waits for OCR. When an act gets its HTML later, the markdown is made from the HTML again.

Without --pdf, task text keeps the texts made from PDFs as they are.

Readers say which texts these are: an act in the api has text.from (html or pdf) with the producer and the source's address, the answer of /api/acts/<journal>/<year>/<pos>/text carries the header X-Text-From, the MCP tool act_text opens such a text with a line naming its PDF, and the viewer puts a note above it.

docs.title: The map of the whole law: map
docs.text:
task map                        # every preset into dataset/map/
task map -- statutes-in-force   # one

All 165 thousand acts with 750 thousand ties are too many for a page, so a preset takes a part of them, with the ties among its acts from dataset/references/:

Preset Acts Ties (2026-11-22) statutes-in-force statutes (ustawy) in force 2,848 / 2,234 statutes every statute since 1918 9,985 / 71,489 in-force every act in force 20,484 / 11,953 statutes-in-force-by-meaning statutes in force that have a vector (task embed), each tied to its 5 nearest by meaning instead of the ties of the source as many as have vectors

ForceAtlas2 places them once, here (about a minute for all three), so a browser only draws: the tab "map of the whole law" of the viewer shows them with sigma.js, /api/map/<preset> gives them. Run task compile first, so the ties are fresh. The files go to Hugging Face with the dataset, so the demo can show them.

docs.title: Search over every year: search:index
docs.text:
task init                                         # once: resources/secrets/typesense_api_key
docker compose --profile search up -d typesense   # Typesense 30.2 on 127.0.0.1:8108
task search:index                                 # titles, types, statuses, keywords
task search:index -- --texts                      # and the first 2000 characters of each text

Every act goes into the collection acts (an act already there is replaced). Titles, keywords and texts are tokenized as Polish. The api answers /api/search?q=...&type=&status=&journal=&page= with acts, the marked words of their texts and counts per type, status and journal. The viewer shows a box "every year" when the search answers. Without Typesense, /api/search answers 503 and says how to start it, and nothing else changes. All 165 thousand acts take 10 seconds; with texts 20 seconds and about 450 MB of memory in the service.

docs.title: Vectors of texts: embed
docs.text:
ollama serve &              # or: docker compose --profile llms up -d llms-ollama
ollama pull bge-m3          # once, about 1.2 GB
task embed                  # every text; task embed -- 2026 for one year

Every act with markdown gets one vector: its title and the first 2000 characters of its text, given to a local multilingual model through Ollama (EMBED_MODEL, bge-m3 by default: 1024 numbers, Polish among its languages). They go beside the texts, in dataset/embeddings/<model>/<journal>/<year>.parquet (ELI, sha256_md, vector), and model.json says how they were made. An act whose markdown did not change keeps its vector, so a run is repeated to take what is new.

DU 2020 (2453 acts) took 1 minute 46 seconds on a GeForce RTX 3060 and 10 MB. All of the law would take about two hours and 670 MB.

docs.title: Search by meaning
docs.text: With the vectors made, task search:index puts them into Typesense too (an existing collection gets the field without being made anew). A search of every year with meaning=1 turns the question into a vector by the same model of Ollama, and Typesense ranks acts by words and by meaning together. A question in English finds Polish acts: "protection of children against violence at school" found the acts of the Minister of Education on safety in schools, where the words alone found one act. Without Ollama, the search says meaning: false and works by words alone. The viewer shows the box "by meaning, in any language" only when the host can do it.

docs.title: Reports to the authorities
docs.text:
Phase 45, the owner's order: reports by mail to the authorities - the Police, the army, CBA, ABW, AW, CERT Polska, NASK. An agent drafts, a person sends: nothing goes out without the owner reading it and saying yes. What is reported and from which mailbox is Q20.

task report:draft                                          # the problems found, drafted with evidence
task report:send -- resources/reports/drafts/<draft>.md    # shown whole, a yes asked, then mailed

docs.title: The authorities
docs.text:
resources/configs/reports/authorities.yaml - official contacts only, each read from the authority's own page, with the day it was read:

Authority Contact Drafts CERT Polska (NASK) the incident form, incydent.cert.pl - its address to be confirmed certificate NASK nask@nask.pl Policja - Centralne Biuro Zwalczania Cyberprzestępczości kontakt.cbzc@cbzc.policja.gov.pl ABW poczta@abw.gov.pl CBA bip@cba.gov.pl Agencja Wywiadu poczta@aw.gov.pl Żandarmeria Wojskowa its page did not answer - to be read again

docs.title: What is drafted
docs.text:
Only what the project can check, with its evidence, checked again when the draft is made - a problem repaired since is not drafted:

  • certificate - a public server whose chain of certificates does not verify. On 2026-11-24 three voivodeships' journals (lubuskie, łódzkie, małopolskie) served a valid certificate without its intermediate one: browsers fetch it themselves, programs reading the journal's API cannot.

A draft is resources/reports/drafts/<date>-<kind>-<host>.md: front matter (to whom, what, the evidence), then the letter in Polish with how to check it (openssl s_client ...).

docs.title: Sending
docs.text: task report:send refuses without a terminal: a person's yes is asked there, after the whole message is shown. It sends from the owner's own mailbox - REPORT_SMTP (smtps://user:password@host:465) and REPORT_FROM in .env - and keeps what was sent in resources/reports/sent/ with its Message-ID. An authority with no confirmed address is never sent to.

docs.title: Gathering on a second machine
docs.text: The whole source is hundreds of thousands of requests and days of work, so the heavy downloading can run on another machine, with the data on an external drive. This page says how to set it up so that it works on any Linux (Parrot OS included) and on any drive, and how to check what comes back. How the data travels home is still open (Q10 in the devlog); both ways are described.

docs.title: The layout that works on any drive
docs.text:
What Where Why The working copy and node_modules the machine's own disk, e.g. ~/__WORKSHOP/forge/sarverott/P-jol-roll npm needs symlinks and executable files, which exFAT and NTFS drives do not keep, and removable drives are usually mounted noexec A bare repository (optional) the external drive a plain remote: git clone /media/<you>/<drive>/P-jol-roll.git; git only reads and writes objects there The gathered data the external drive, through RESOURCES_DIR big files, written whole (.part first), nothing in it is ever run 
# on the second machine
git clone https://github.com/Sarverott/P-jol-roll.git ~/__WORKSHOP/forge/sarverott/P-jol-roll
cd ~/__WORKSHOP/forge/sarverott/P-jol-roll
npm install                                   # Node 24, npm 11 (.nvmrc)
mkdir -p /media/$USER/<drive>/p-jol-roll-resources
cp resources/.map.json resources/frontends.json /media/$USER/<drive>/p-jol-roll-resources/
echo "RESOURCES_DIR=/media/$USER/<drive>/p-jol-roll-resources" >> .env
task check                                    # nothing asks the internet
task gather -- 2026 --acts --limit 5          # a small run first

.env.example lists every setting; every task reads .env of the working copy (dotenv in Taskfile.yml), so RESOURCES_DIR set there holds for all of them; a variable set in the shell wins over it. npm run ... without Task does not read .env: there, export the variable first. .env is ignored by git.

docs.title: When something refuses
docs.text:
What you see Cause What to do fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository git refuses a repository whose files belong to another user; on exFAT and NTFS every file seems to belong to whoever mounted the drive git config --global --add safe.directory /media/<you>/<drive>/P-jol-roll.git for that one path; better, keep the working copy on the internal disk npm install fails with EPERM or symlink errors the filesystem of the drive has no symlinks (exFAT, FAT32) install on the internal disk (the layout above) Permission denied when a hook, tsx or task runs the drive is mounted noexec (findmnt -o TARGET,OPTIONS <path> shows it) do not run anything from the drive; only data lives there no task binary after npm install npm 11 skips install scripts that are not approved package.json approves @go-task/cli in allowScripts; if it was installed by hand with an older checkout, run npm install again hooks do not stop a bad commit @go-task/cli older than 3.54 drops the exit code npm install from this version of the repository brings 3.54

lsblk -f shows how a drive is formatted, findmnt <path> how it is mounted. task unittesting:parrot-os-drive shows the three refusals above on Parrot OS with a FAT drive mounted noexec, and the layout of this page working on the same drive.

docs.title: Bringing the data back
docs.text:
The second machine gathers, then seals, so every file it took has a checksum record in dataset/files/:

task seal            # records for anything gathered without one
task seal -- --check # reads every file again, names any that differ

Then one of two ways (Q10):

  • It pushes to Hugging Face itself, with the owner's token in .env: task resources:push -- bucket, task resources:push -- dataset. The home machine takes it with task resources:pull -- dataset (and bucket when it wants the raw files), then task seal -- --check.
  • The drive travels home: point RESOURCES_DIR at it there, run task seal -- --check, then push from home.

Either way, a file with a record is not asked for again, so two machines that share the dataset do not gather the same files twice. Split the work by journal or by years (task gather -- 1990 1991 --acts --limit 0 --publisher MP) when both machines gather at once.

docs.title: Other sources
docs.text:
The journals say what the law is. Two more sources say how it was made and how it is applied. Each has its own command, and all of them write into the one dataset (tables, the training collection) and the one bucket (raw files), each source in a directory of its own (phase 10).

Command Source Local directories gather ELI API of Sejm: the journals resources/dataset, resources/bucket sejm API of Sejm's work: processes and prints resources/dataset/sejm, resources/bucket/sejm saos SAOS: court judgments resources/dataset/SAOS

So task resources:push -- dataset and -- bucket send every source. Before phase 10 they had directories of their own (sejm-dataset, sejm-bucket, saos-dataset); task resources:merge moves what was gathered there inside, never over a file that is there already.

docs.title: Work of Sejm: sejm
docs.text:
task sejm                              # tables of the current term
task sejm -- 9 10                      # of these terms
task sejm -- --all                     # of every term
task sejm -- 10 --files --limit 50     # and 50 files that are not here yet

Source: https://api.sejm.gov.pl/sejm, the same host and the same manners as the journals. Prints exist for terms 6 to 10 (2007 until now); term 10 had 3426 prints on 2026-10-13.

File What it is dataset/sejm/terms.json terms of Sejm with their dates dataset/sejm/term10/processes.jsonl legislative processes, one per line dataset/sejm/term10/prints.jsonl prints, one per line, with names of their files bucket/sejm/term10/processes/<number>.json one process with its stages: referrals to committees, readings and what followed bucket/sejm/term10/prints/<number>/<file> files of a print: the draft with its justification, opinions

A process that ended with a published act carries the ELI and address of that act, so processes attach to the acts of the journals directly. The justification inside a print is the authors' own explanation of what the draft is for.

--files takes details of processes first, then files of prints. --limit counts files, 20 by default. What is here is not asked for again. Tables are written again on every run.

Not gathered yet: votings, interpellations, committees, members.

docs.title: The sittings of Sejm: sittings
docs.text:
A day's statements take the API 25 s and more to give (40 s timed out on 2026-11-24): they are given two minutes, and a day whose statements still do not come is taken as one PDF, bucket/sejm/term10/transcripts/<sitting>/<date>.pdf (phase 41); an act's debates say so (pdf: true).

The work of Sejm as discussion (phase 35): the sittings of a term, and what was said on each of their days.

task sittings                           # the days of the current term that are not here, 20 at most
task sittings -- 10 --files --limit 40  # and the texts of the statements, 40 days then 40 texts
File What it holds dataset/sejm/term10/sittings.json the sittings, each with its days (/proceedings) dataset/sejm/term10/transcripts/<sitting>/<date>.json the statements of a day: who spoke, as whom, from which club, when bucket/sejm/term10/transcripts/<sitting>/<date>/<num>.html the text of one statement

A day after today is not asked for, nor a sitting numbered 0 (planned). A day is known from its file, so a run takes only what is missing.

The acts tie to them through their processes: a stage of a process read on a sitting (sittingNum, date) names the day; the statements of that day are about everything on its agenda, and one whose text names a print of the bill (druk nr 1111) is marked as about it. Every interface shows it: the act's page (in Sejm), /api/acts/DU/2025/637/debates, the MCP tool act_debates, task do -- act-debates DU/2025/637.

docs.title: Court judgments: saos
docs.text:
task saos -- 2025                  # 3 months of 2025 that are not here yet
task saos -- 2020 2021 --limit 0   # every month of these years
task saos -- --quality             # judgments SAOS dates after today or before 1918, kept apart

Source: https://www.saos.org.pl/api, System Analizy Orzeczeń Sądowych. It holds 543 thousand judgments (2026-10-13) of common courts, the Supreme Court, the Constitutional Tribunal, the National Appeal Chamber and administrative courts, with full texts.

Remember! SAOS is not a server of the state. It collects judgments that courts publish. Who runs it today and under what terms the data may be republished was not checked. [TODO] It is asked more slowly: 30 requests per minute by default. It sits inside the dataset now, so task resources:push -- dataset sends it: decide about publishing before gathering it into a dataset that is pushed.

One file per month, by date of judgment: dataset/SAOS/judgments/2025/2025-01.jsonl, one judgment per line, as the API gave it. Fields that matter most here:

Field Meaning id number of the judgment in SAOS courtType, judgmentType, judgmentDate which court, what kind, when courtCases case numbers textContent the full text referencedRegulations acts the judgment refers to, with year and position of the journal source where SAOS took it from

referencedRegulations is what attaches a judgment to the acts: it gives journalYear and journalEntry, which is DU/<year>/<entry>.

A month is taken whole, page by page, and written when its last page arrived. Only months that ended are taken; the running month would be kept as a half of itself. A month that is here is not asked for again, so judgments added later to an old month are missed until its file is deleted. --limit counts months, 3 by default.

Dates in SAOS are sometimes wrong (a judgment dated in year 208, another in 3013). Those fall outside any year you would ask for.

Judgments name judges and case numbers. Parties are anonymised by the courts before publication.

Until phase 41 SAOS refused every page of the crawler with 406: crawlee asked for HTML, SAOS gives only JSON. Every walk now asks for JSON first. SAOS holds judgments dated in years that cannot be (3013, 2101, 208); no month asks for them, so --quality takes them on their own into judgments/misdated.jsonl and counts them in SAOS/quality.json. SAOS is fed from the common courts' Portal Orzeczeń, which has no public API (Q25).

docs.title: What else was looked at
docs.text: See ideas, "Other government sources in Poland": the open data portal, the court register, statistics and the national bank answer, and are data about the country and not law. They have no command yet.

docs.title: The law of the European Union: eu
docs.text:
The law of the EU binds Poland since 2004 (phase 42). Its acts come from the Publications Office of the EU: the lists from its SPARQL endpoint (CELLAR), the texts in Polish by content negotiation.

task eu -- 2016 2024                # every act of these years, their Polish titles
task eu -- 2016 --texts --limit 50  # and the Polish texts of acts in force, 50 at most
task international                  # the agreements the journals of the state published
File What it holds dataset/EU/acts/2024.jsonl an act per line: CELEX, date, kind (REG, DIR, DEC, REG_IMPL, CORRIGENDUM, ...), in force, Polish title, ELI bucket/EU/2024/<CELEX>.xhtml its text in Polish, as the Office gives it (only acts in force, never a corrigendum) dataset/international/agreements.jsonl the agreements, conventions, protocols, treaties, documents ending them and government statements of Dziennik Ustaw and Monitor Polski, from the listings here

The treaties (CELEX 1...) and the secondary law (3...). 2024 holds 3,765 acts, 2,310 of them in force (2026-11-24). Read them with MCP eu_law and agreements, /api/eu/<year>, /api/eu/act/<CELEX>, /api/agreements. How far international law goes - the CJEU, the ECtHR, the UN's treaties - is Q22.

docs.title: Local and regional law: regional
docs.text:
The official journals of the sixteen voivodeships (phase 43): resolutions of communes, districts and regions, orders of voivodes - local law. The list is resources/configs/regional/journals.yaml, from dziennikiurzedowe.gov.pl.

task regional                                           # every journal asked what it is, the newest year of each
task regional -- POL_WOJ_LB --year 2025 --files --limit 50   # one journal, a year, the PDFs of its acts

Ten of them run one platform whose API answers as the Sejm's ELI API does (/api/eli/acts/<code>/<year>): over a million acts since 2010. The state of every journal is kept in dataset/regional/journals.json. On 2026-11-24:

Journal State dolnośląskie, lubelskie, opolskie, podkarpackie, pomorskie, śląskie, świętokrzyskie, warmińsko-mazurskie, wielkopolskie, zachodniopomorskie answer: POL_WOJ_DS, _LB, _OP, _PK, _PM, _SL, _SK, _WM, _WP, _ZP lubuskie, łódzkie, małopolskie an incomplete chain of certificates (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE) mazowieckie does not answer in 30 s (an HTTP/2 error to curl) kujawsko-pomorskie, podlaskie another platform, not the ELI API

docs.title: Public tenders: tenders
docs.text:
What the state buys (phase 43): every notice of e-Zamówienia (the Biuletyn Zamówień Publicznych) and the EU's TED notices with a buyer in Poland.

task tenders -- 2026-11-20          # one day: both sources
task tenders -- 2026-11 --limit 0   # every day of a month that ended
File What it holds dataset/tenders/BZP/2026/2026-11-20.jsonl the notices of the day, every kind (contract, result, plan, update, ...) bucket/tenders/BZP/2026/2026-11-20/<objectId>.html a notice's own text dataset/tenders/TED/2026/2026-11-20.jsonl TED's notices with a buyer in Poland

e-Zamówienia's API ignores its page number and the time of its end date: it gives the first 100 notices from the moment asked, oldest first. So a day is read as a cursor - asked again from the last notice's moment until fewer than 100 come back (phase 44 found it: splitting the window, as phase 43 did, never shrinks it). Its firewall refused a burst of requests with 403 once: requests go three seconds apart, a refusal is waited out a minute, and a day that still fails is said and left for the next run.

docs.title: Torrents pointed to by IPFS
docs.text:
The first step of M5, no centre (phase 37): the dataset and the bucket shared as torrents, and the torrents found through IPFS - so the law of Poland gathered here does not depend on one host.

task torrents -- -only dataset   # 12 torrents of the dataset (4.6 GB), 18 s here
task torrents                    # and the bucket's, a torrent per journal and year (189 GB, once)
task torrents:publish            # the owner's move: put on IPFS (asks first)

How it holds together:

  1. Hugging Face hosts the files. Every torrent carries a web seed (BEP 19) pointing at the same files there, so a BitTorrent client (qBittorrent, Transmission, ...) downloads it even with no peer.
  2. Peers share it on. Whoever keeps a torrent seeds it; peers meet by DHT, or by trackers given in TORRENT_TRACKERS.
  3. IPFS points to the torrents. The torrents and index.json (each torrent's magnet link, infohash, size, CID) form one directory whose root CID is where they are found: ipfs://<ROOT>/index.json.

Everything is made offline by the Go stack (stacks/go, pjolseed): the CIDs are those ipfs add -r --cid-version=1 gives, checked against kubo, and torrents.car holds every block. task torrents:publish starts the IPFS node of compose (profile ipfs, kubo, its swarm on port 4001), imports the CAR and pins it - publishing, so it is the owner's, as pushing to Hugging Face is.

A torrent whose files did not change is kept: after a gathering, only the years that grew are hashed again, and the root CID changes with them.

The details: the Go stack's README.

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: The owner's idea (Q15, changelog phase 12): pages are not rewritten with names of texts and loaders. Their text nodes are found, hooked by a SHA-256 of what they say, and their content is replaced from a language pack. Phase 16 checked it first, in src/i18n/ with tests/i18n.test.ts. This page says what came out.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
"115 acts"  -> normalized, numbers as holes -> "{0} acts" -> SHA-256 -> 6f1c...e2
pack PL-PL: "6f1c...e2": { "one": "{0} akt", "few": "{0} akty", "many": "{0} aktów" }
            -> "115 aktów"
  • src/i18n/sha256.ts: SHA-256, synchronous, the same in a browser, in node and in a terminal (checked against node's own).
  • src/i18n/hooks.ts: hookOf(text), translate(pack, text), and t(pack, text) for a terminal: the pack's text, or the English when the pack has none. A number in a text is a hole, so "3 acts" and "115 acts" are one entry; an entry can hold the plural forms of its language (Intl.PluralRules), chosen by the first number.
  • src/i18n/dom.ts: collect(root) gives every hook of a page with its English template (that is how the default pack is made), apply(root, pack) lays a pack over the page, and apply(root, undefined) gives the English back, which is remembered per node. follow(root, pack) keeps the pack over what a framework renders later.

docs.title: What is translated: what is marked
docs.text:
Since phase 21 a page names what is its interface, by classes; nothing else is touched:

Class Translated i18n-texts-slot every text under the element, and the readable attributes of what is under it i18n-texts-placeholder the placeholder of this element i18n-texts-title / i18n-texts-alt / i18n-texts-label its title / alt / aria-label

Inside a slot, data stays under translate="no" and code is skipped. The introduction is one slot (its <main>), the viewer marks its parts one by one, and the documentation is marked as one slot by its builder.

docs.title: What works
docs.text:
Checked How text nodes and the attributes people read (placeholder, title, aria-label, alt) a page in linkedom numbers and plural forms (1 akt, 3 akty, 115 aktów) t() and the page only what is marked by the classes above; inside it, data is never translated: titles and texts of acts sit under translate="no", the attribute HTML has for it; code and pre are skipped too the page back to English, or to another language, without reloading the page what Vue renders later: a text node written again holds English, the observer translates it again; the English it remembered is dropped jsdom, as a browser one pack for every interface: the same hook in a page, the launcher and the CLI t() takes plain strings

Vue patches a text node by writing its nodeValue only when its own virtual text changes, and it never reads the DOM back. A translated node therefore stays translated until Vue writes it again, and then the observer translates it again. The page and the framework do not fight.

docs.title: What does not, and what is done about it
docs.text:
• A sentence cut by markup ("the PDF at the source is the text") gives fragments, each hooked alone. Word order differs between languages, so fragments translate badly. Such sentences get their own short wording, or an element marked as one unit later on.
  • The same English, two meanings ("status" as a column and as a state) is one hook. When it matters, the element gets data-i18n-context, which salts the hook (not needed yet).
  • Changing the English orphans its translation, because the hook changes. The pack keeps the English of every entry, so the script that makes packs finds orphans and translates the new English again; old entries are dropped.
  • Search engines do not see a translation made in the browser. The introduction and the documentation are therefore translated when the website is built, by the same apply() over the built HTML, into /<language>/ copies. The viewer is translated in the browser.
  • The English flashes before a pack arrives. The pack is loaded before the viewer mounts.

So the idea holds, with no texts named in code: the pages stay as written, the interface is marked by classes and data by a standard attribute, and one small library serves the browser and the terminal.

docs.title: Language packs
docs.text:
resources/locales/ holds a JSON file per language, listed in resources/locales/.index.json with EN-US the default. Since phase 28 it is a git submodule: the packs live in their own gist (0b86ecd07d55426754759bdff5550d87), the source the project reads - a fresh clone takes it by git submodule update --init resources/locales (task i18n:pull), and task init says when it is missing.

Pack Made by EN-US.json task i18n:collect: the built introduction and viewer opened in a headless browser, their own runtime collects every text with its hook PL-PL.json, UK-UA.json, DE-DE.json task i18n:translate: argostranslate (the engine of LibreTranslate), models downloaded once 
task web:build && npm run --prefix webpage build    # both pages built
task i18n:collect                                   # their English -> EN-US.json
task i18n:translate                                 # what the other packs miss
task i18n:translate -- PL-PL --again                # one pack anew (not its reviewed entries)
task i18n:publish -- "the texts of phase 28"        # committed in the gist, pushed, the submodule staged

A pack changed here (collected, translated or reviewed by a person) reaches everyone only after task i18n:publish: the gist gets the commit, and this repository the submodule's new commit with the next step. The workflows that build take the packs by git submodule update --init resources/locales.

  • A text with a number is translated once per plural form of the language, with the number that form takes (plural in the index: Polish one 1, few 3, many 5), and the number becomes the hole again.
  • Names in keep of the index (Dziennik Ustaw, Sejm, SAOS, P_JOL_ROLL...) are never translated: they stand in as numbers while the model works, because letters get transliterated by some models and numbers never do.
  • Machine translation makes mistakes ("Bucket" became "Bukiet"). A person fixes an entry in the pack and lists its hook in reviewed. The script never overwrites a reviewed entry and never drops it.
  • A language is added by a line in the index (with its argos pair) and task i18n:translate.

The viewer and the introduction take the pack of ?lang=PL-PL, else the last choice, else the browser's languages, else English. They load only that pack and lay it over the page before it shows, and a switch in the header changes it without a reload.

The documentation is translated when the website is built (scripts/devops/pages/build.sh runs src/devtools/docs-i18n.ts): the built MkDocs site is copied into site/docs/pl-pl/, uk-ua/ and de-de/, and each pack is laid over the guides, the glossary and the home page by the same apply() the browser uses. The changelog and the devlog stay in English in every copy, because they keep the owner's words word for word. Every page gets a list of languages in its header, pointing at the same page in each copy. Read the Docs builds only the English.

Identifiers are never translated: a text that is one path or name (datasets/Sarverott/polish_national_law_docs) gets no hook, and one inside a sentence (resources/.map.json, SHA-256, v0.11.0) stands in as a number while the model works, like the names of keep.

docs.title: The terminal
docs.text:
The launcher (bare task), its REPL and the lists of tasks speak the language of the terminal: P_JOL_ROLL_LANG=PL-PL task, else LANG (pl_PL.UTF-8 gives PL-PL), else English. The descriptions of the tasks are the manual of the CLI, so they are translated too.

In code a text is written once, in English, through tr() (src/i18n/terminal.ts):

tr("task {name} ended with {code}", { name, code })

The English is the hook, as on pages. Named places in braces are filled after the pack is laid over, so a translation puts them where its language wants them. While the model works they stand in as numbers, like quoted commands ("list", "gather -- 2026"), so neither is translated. task i18n:collect finds every tr("...") of src/ and the description of every task by itself. Tests run in English whatever LANG the machine has (vitest.config.ts).

docs.title: The declaration of transparency
docs.text:
Phase 44, the owner's order: every public office with its official contacts - e-mail, phone, address, ePUAP - placed on OpenStreetMap, and the address space of the state. Institutions only: what an office publishes as its own contact. No named person's private data (Q24).

task python:offices                    # the official contact bases of dane.gov.pl, into one table
task python:geocode -- --limit 3000    # the offices with no coordinates, placed by Nominatim (about an hour)
task python:networks                   # the state's networks and autonomous systems in RIPE
File What it holds dataset/transparency/offices.jsonl an office per line: name, kind, voivodeship, district, town, street, number, postal code, phones, fax, e-mails, www, ePUAP, latitude, longitude (and osm when Nominatim placed it), where it came from dataset/transparency/geocode.json every address Nominatim was asked, with what it said - asked once dataset/transparency/networks.jsonl a network (inetnum, inet6num) or an autonomous system (aut-num) per line, with its organisation's RIPE key and name

docs.title: The offices
docs.text: resources/configs/transparency/sources.yaml names the resources of dane.gov.pl, the open data of the state: the voivodes' combined administration (with its services: police, fire brigade, inspections), the tax administration (KAS), the civil registry offices, the Polish posts abroad. Each is a CSV or a spreadsheet with columns of its own; a column is told by its words (telefon, e-mail, miejscowość, szerokość geograficzna...). On 2026-11-24: 4,933 offices, 4,921 with an e-mail, all with a phone, 1,929 with coordinates from their source. More sources are added to the file the same way.

docs.title: Their places
docs.text: An office with no coordinates is asked of Nominatim, OpenStreetMap's geocoder: structured (street, town, postal code), then by words; one request a second, as its policy asks; every answer cached, so a run asks only what is new. docs.title: The address space of the state
docs.text:
The organisations of the RIPE database in Poland whose e-mail is in gov.pl, or whose name has a public word (Ministerstwo, Urząd, Gmina, Starostwo, Komenda, Prokuratura, Sąd...), and every network and autonomous system registered to them. Only the organisation's key and name are kept - a RIPE object also names people, and they are left out. On 2026-11-24: 89 organisations, 108 networks (84 IPv4, 24 IPv6), 82 autonomous systems.

Read in every interface: MCP transparency (of: offices or networks), /api/transparency/offices?q=Lublin, /api/transparency/networks.
